title: Exact same-model cache View algebra versus approximate cross-model translation
hypothesis: A position-shift View within one RoPE-only Pythia model can be served exactly from one canonical position-neutral KV cache using a low-description phase code, while an unrelated SmolLM2 consumer requires an approximate learned cross-model mapper with nonzero quality cost. The experiment distinguishes exact algebraic Views from approximate translators rather than treating both as the same kind of cache reuse.
prior_art_boundary: PA156 provides direct prior art for deferred positional encoding and one physical cache serving logical placements. PA157/PA236 establish learned cross-model ridge translation as approximate, pair-dependent prior art. This experiment is a small local audit, not a reproduction of those systems.

data.exclusion: Exclude all Wikitext-2 titles/rows and all prompt title/text hashes reserved by MA-883 and MA-886.
data.article_split: Whole article title hash mod 4; bucket0 development, buckets1/2/3 fresh seeds 11887/11891/11897.
data.prompt_alignment: Require exact character offset alignment and equal token counts for Pythia70 and SmolLM2.
data.split: 24 map-fit, 8 check, 16 test; exact-algebra evaluation uses held-out test rows; cross-model ridge fits only map-fit rows.

fixed_design.exact_view: Pythia-70M has RoPE-only positional dependence. Remove source RoPE from each cached key to create the canonical position-neutral K; apply phase shift Δ=17 to cached keys, and supply shifted position_ids to the final target query. Compare full shifted-sequence logits/NLL against canonical-cache query and against a separately shifted native prefill.
fixed_design.approximate_view: Fit ordinary independent per-target-role affine ridge maps from Pythia-70M prefix K/V to SmolLM2 prefix K/V, nearest-relative layer/head matching, source/target inverse RoPE for keys and target RoPE restoration.
fixed_design.exact_phase_code: One signed int32 Δ=17 plus fixed-format metadata. No learned degrees of freedom.
fixed_design.context: One-token next-token replay; exact test covers native sequence at positions 0..n and globally shifted positions Δ..Δ+n.

controls: Native Pythia-70M prefill at position offset 0
Native Pythia-70M prefill at position offset 17
Canonical KV cache with phase-shift View algebra
Independent full affine Pythia70→Smol ridge mapper
success_gate: Treating the exact position transform as an FP32 algebraic identity, require same-model View max absolute logit difference <=0.02 and absolute NLL delta <=0.005 in every fresh prompt; serialized exact View metadata is <=1% of one materialized K-cache byte count. Approximate cross-model row is reported separately and is never labeled exact. Report cache transform MAC proxy and CPU wall time.
failure_gate: Any exactness gate miss. Independently classify the approximate translator by +1 nat target quality, mapper bytes, and translation/replay latency; approximate failure does not erase an exact algebra pass.

storage.cache_state: Report canonical K/V, materialized shifted K, and target cache bytes separately; shared model weights are common within exact same-model comparison.

scope: One Pythia model, one known RoPE global-shift symmetry, one approximate Pythia70→SmolLM2 pair, one-token replay.
No general exact cross-model equivalence, no multi-token rollout, and no GPU fused LazyAttention claim.
protocol_amendments: Before any development metrics were written: fixed cache plumbing to convert CPU NumPy K/V arrays to batch-first Torch tensors before DynamicCache injection. The first development process raised a type error before scoring; no method, metric, data split, or decision rule changed. Fresh data remained unopened.

A second development-only run exposed an extra batch dimension on the native legacy-cache path, before any scores were written. Cache injection now accepts both unbatched array K/V and already-batched Torch K/V while normalizing them to rank 4. No method, data, metric, or decision rule changed; fresh remains sealed.

Before fresh access, development showed FP32 full-model replay accumulation up to 0.0152 logit and 0.0027 nat while layer cache/key algebra matched within about 1e-5. The exact-view output tolerance was set to 0.02 logits and 0.005 nat to bound FP32 accumulation; data, model, transform, and quality metric are unchanged. No fresh results had been opened.
